summary: Dense teak-and-bamboo forest on the Purna river — one of Gujarat's rainiest tracts, with forest drives, trails and the Mahal campsite at its heart.
description:
Purna Wildlife Sanctuary protects a big block of moist deciduous forest around the Purna river in northern Dang — by most measures the wettest, densest forest tract in Gujarat. Towering teak, huge bamboo brakes and a closed canopy give it a feel closer to the Western Ghats than anything else in the state.

Wildlife here is heard more than seen: leopard, hyena and jungle cat move through, but realistic sightings are barking deer, four-horned antelope, wild boar, giant squirrels, and a strong bird list — hornbills, woodpeckers, raptors and winter migrants. The experience is the forest itself: drives on the internal roads, guided walks around Mahal, and the river running brown in monsoon and clear in winter. The Mahal eco-campsite deep inside the sanctuary is the natural base, with forest-department cottages and tents.

Entry works via forest-department permits at the range gates, with local guides assigned for walks. Seasonal closures apply — the core is typically restricted during peak monsoon — so check before building a trip around it.
highlights: Teak and giant bamboo under a closed canopy
Strong birding: hornbills to winter migrants
Mahal eco-campsite as an in-forest base

modes.road: Entry via the Mahal road from Ahwa or from the Waghai side; internal forest roads are unpaved
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Forest tracks to Mahal; walks are guided from the campsite/range office
access.road_condition: Approach tarred; internal roads dirt — slow, and slippery in rain; 4WD helps after rainfall

parking.notes: At Mahal campsite and range gates

timings.note: Daylight entry via permit gates; varies with conditions

fees.note: Per person; some sources cite higher bundled rates — conflicting

booking.notes: Day entry at the gate; Mahal campsite stays book via the forest department

visit.notes: Core-area access is typically restricted in peak monsoon (roughly mid-June to September) — verify current rules before planning.

seasonality.notes: October–March is prime: open roads, active birdlife, comfortable walking. Monsoon transforms the forest but limits access.

experience.photography_notes: Forest is dark under canopy — fast lenses or high ISO; winter mornings give mist over the Purna for landscape frames.

amenities.food: Meals at Mahal campsite when booked; otherwise carry food — Ahwa has the nearest restaurants
amenities.guides: Local guides assigned at the gate/campsite; mandatory for walks

warnings: Stay with your guide on all walks — this is leopard country
No off-track driving; exit the sanctuary before dark
Leeches are standard issue in and just after monsoon

emergency.police: Ahwa PS; forest range office Mahal

tips: Book Mahal campsite ahead and build the day around a dawn walk
Pair with Girmal Falls — the road onward is one of Dang's best forest drives
Winter nights get cold in the forest; pack accordingly

faqs.a: Very unlikely — they're present but shy. Come for the forest, the birds and the deer; treat any big-cat pugmarks your guide finds as the win.
